historical_references.reference: Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Mauryan Empire in India, was named Chandru (Chandragupta) after the moon god, Chandrama.
historical_references.context: Chandragupta Maurya was a powerful ruler who expanded his empire to cover most of the Indian subcontinent. He defeated the previous Nanda Emperor and established the Mauryan Empire. His name, Chandragupta, means 'moon-born' and is derived from the name of the moon god, Chandrama.
